title: The Safehouse of Marseille's old port
premise: Xanthe Montrose, a freelance interpreter who has spent six years erasing herself from every database, is shaken when the Marseille safehouse she secretly owns appears on a real-estate site with interior photos — including her hidden document cache. The listing is bait: someone inside the failing peace delegation has traced her, and an attack planned to look like a gas explosion will kill the delegation and crater European markets at Frankfurt's opening bell. Forced out of hiding, Xanthe assembles an unlikely crew — a disgraced port inspector, a teenage hacker squatting in her building, and the one delegate she trusts — to expose the plot before dawn. She succeeds, but at the cost of surrendering her anonymity to French authorities, and she discovers that survival was never the same thing as living.
about_author: Edmund Reyes is a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent a decade in Mediterranean port cities before turning to fiction full-time. He writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped between institutions, and lives quietly in Lisbon with a dog named after a customs form.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Scrolling property listings after a brutal negotiation session, Xanthe finds her own safehouse for sale — twelve photos deep, a shot of the loose floorboard under which she keeps forged identities and delegation memos. She realizes whoever took the photos had keys. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath practiced calm; her invisibility was an illusion sold to the highest bidder.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Rules
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Flashbacks interleave with the present as she executes her evacuation protocol, but hesitation creeps in — the café owner, the neighbor girl Léna, the life she pretended wasn't hers. At the safehouse she finds the cache disturbed: one file missing, a copy of the delegation's security schedule. Emotional beat: grief for a self she's about to burn.

chapters.title: The Man Who Bought a Doorway
chapters.summary: POV: Karim Daoud, disgraced port inspector turned fixer. Karim admits he brokered the sale anonymously to pay debts, unaware of the buyer — a shell company tied to Meridian Logistics. He offers Xanthe his files in exchange for not naming him. Emotional beat: two compromised people negotiating trust with nothing but leverage.

chapters.title: Interpreting Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Back inside the peace delegation, Xanthe works a closed session and notices a delegate, Voss, translating numbers instead of arguments — delivery windows disguised as tariff figures. She records nothing, says nothing, and hates herself for it. Emotional beat: the interpreter's oldest sin — precision without courage.

chapters.title: Léna Knows the Wi-Fi
chapters.summary: POV: Léna, sixteen, squatter and hacker. Léna traces the shell company through Meridian to a Frankfurt clearing desk betting heavily against European stability by Thursday morning. She brings it to Xanthe not out of heroism but because 'you looked like someone keeping secrets badly.' Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, the first spark of found family.

chapters.title: What the Markets Want
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Xanthe/Karim. The picture assembles: the attack on the delegation's closing dinner will be timed as a gas main rupture, triggering panic selling before Frankfurt opens — profit for whoever holds the short positions. Karim identifies the inside man: Voss. Emotional beat: vertigo of scale — small lives weighed against billions.

chapters.title: The Price of Being Nobody
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Voss corners Xanthe, revealing he's known her real name for months and offering her exit: silence, money, a new identity better than the one she built. For one night she almost takes it. Emotional beat: temptation — the corruption theme turned inward, power buying exactly what she always wanted.

chapters.title: Gaslight at the Old Port
chapters.summary: POV: ensemble, converging. The team splits: Léna feeds false confirmation to the plotters, Karim gets the harbor authority to 'inspect' the gas lines publicly, forcing the attackers to accelerate. Xanthe walks into the closing dinner wearing her interpreter badge like armor. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose; no plan survives contact.

chapters.title: Thursday, Before the Bell
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Climax. During the toast, Xanthe interprets Voss's coded remarks aloud — exposing the operation in front of delegates and a hidden recorder — while Karim's inspection forces the bomb crew to abort rather than detonate early. Voss is taken; the markets open flat. But a Meridian cleaner comes for Xanthe in the stairwell, and Léna's warning saves her life. Emotional beat: victory purchased with exposure.

chapters.title: A Name, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Epilogue. Under formal inquiry, Xanthe gives investigators her true name for the first time in six years — the price of survival finally paid in full. She keeps the apartment above the café, teaches Léna encryption over cheap wine, and unpacks the go-bag into drawers. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; found family replacing the fortress self.
